commit.message:
Upgrade recommendation engine with an offline agentic, eval-gated pipeline

Delivers expert-quality advice to the free, on-device product at zero
per-user cost by moving the LLM to build time (Claude Max plan, no
metered API):

- tools/generate_plan_library.py: an offline agentic workflow. Opus 4.7
  authors the full library (5 axes x 3 severities x 4 tiers x 3 options
  = 180 actions) via one-shot `claude -p` calls routed through the local
  OAuth session. The EvalCritic agent (Opus) vets every (axis, severity)
  for tone + medical-advice safety, and a deterministic blocklist scans
  every line. Nothing is written unless it passes. `--check` re-validates
  the shipped file with no LLM calls.
- web/lib/plan-library.generated.json: the vetted output, shipped as
  static data. Runtime selection stays pure and deterministic — no
  network, no inference, scales to any number of users for free.
- web/lib/plan.ts: rewired to select by axis AND severity, so advice
  intensity scales with how low each axis scored.
- regression.yml: CI now runs the library safety gate (schema + blocklist)
  on every push, so the shipped content can never drift unsafe.

The gate proved itself during generation: the EvalCritic rejected a first
pass that stacked "see a dermatologist" referrals as medical advice.

Verified: --check clean (180 items), pnpm typecheck clean, pnpm build green.

commit.message:
Add in-app usage logging + feedback for the public beta

Goal: validate demand with ~400-500 real users at zero cost before any
server spend. A static app can't show aggregate usage on its own, so we
log named events to a free analytics backend (PostHog, ~1M events/mo
free) that the operator reads as funnels/retention.

Privacy-first for a face app:
- The selfie and its pixels never leave the device; we send event names
  plus small non-PII props only (score bucket, source, framing reason).
- Cookieless (localStorage persistence) so no consent banner is needed.
- Autocapture and session recording disabled; only the named events fire.

Mechanism:
- lib/analytics.ts: env-gated wrapper. With NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY unset
  every call is a silent no-op, so local dev and the app are unaffected.
  Single AppEvent union is the source of truth for the funnel.
- AnalyticsProvider: boots once, logs a pageview per route change.
- Funnel instrumented end to end: checkin_opened -> camera_ready/blocked
  -> framing_rejected -> completed -> result_viewed -> plan_tier_opened /
  unlock_clicked -> history_viewed, plus feedback_opened/submitted/dismissed.

In-app feedback (FeedbackCard on the result screen): 1-5 rating, three
signal chips (believable / useful / would-use-daily), optional note.
Captures the accuracy, value, and retention signals that decide whether
to invest. Shown once, then suppressed via a localStorage flag.

Deploy workflow passes NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY/HOST from repo variables;
checkin privacy line now discloses anonymous usage logging.

Verified: pnpm typecheck clean, pnpm build green on all routes.

commit.message:
Deploy the web app to GitHub Pages from CI (zero local build)

The app must ship without building on a restricted laptop. Configure
Next.js for static export and add a GitHub Actions workflow that builds
web/ on GitHub's runners and publishes to GitHub Pages. No third-party
account, no local toolchain.

- next.config.mjs: output "export", trailingSlash, images.unoptimized,
  and a NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH-driven basePath/assetPrefix so the project
  site works under /mirror-score/.
- app/manifest.ts replaces the static manifest.json so icon URLs and
  start_url pick up the base path.
- .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile +
  pnpm build with NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/mirror-score, upload-pages-artifact,
  deploy-pages. Triggers on push to main and the feature branch, plus
  manual dispatch.

Verified locally: export produces out/ with all assets, manifest icons,
start_url, and internal links correctly prefixed under /mirror-score/.

commit.message:
Make the web app fully functional at zero cost

Hard constraint: the product must run without spending anything — no API
keys, no database, no payment processor, no paid hosting. Re-architected
the web app to be entirely self-contained and client-side.

On-device analysis (lib/analyze.ts):
- Reads the captured selfie's pixels on a canvas and derives the five
  axes with pure math. Deterministic, offline, $0.
- skin_clarity from texture variance; hydration from a luminance bell;
  redness/calmness from cheek-vs-forehead redness excess; dark_circles
  from under-eye/cheek luminance ratio; freshness as a composite.
- framingQuality() gates too-dark / too-bright / no-face frames.
- Validated on synthetic ImageData: red cheeks drop calmness to 0,
  dullness drops hydration to 22, dark under-eyes drop that axis to 0.

Rule-based plan (lib/plan.ts):
- Curated wellness-action library keyed by axis, graded by time horizon.
- Ranks axes and builds the tiered plan weakest-first. No LLM call.

Local persistence (lib/storage.ts):
- History + settings in localStorage. 1 free check-in/day enforced.
- "Free during beta" unlock flag in place of real payments.

Screens wired end to end:
- /checkin captures via getUserMedia OR photo upload, runs analysis,
  saves, routes to result. Daily-limit gate for free users.
- /result reads the real latest check-in (sample fallback), with a
  working beta-unlock for the 7d/30d tiers.
- /history: Glow-Score trend sparkline + per-day list, gated behind unlock.

Backend (src/) stays as the future premium LLM path; not required to ship.

Build green; all four routes prerender and return 200.

commit.message:
v0.2 UI scaffold: Next.js 14 PWA with editorial-clinical design

Monorepo: backend stays in src/, frontend lands in web/.

Stack:
- Next.js 14 App Router + TypeScript strict + Tailwind + lucide-react
- Three colors total: bone (#FAF8F5) / ink (#1F1A17) / rose (#D4847A)
- Two type families (Inter + Inter Display); five sizes max
- One animation (score count-up); respects prefers-reduced-motion
- PWA manifest + 192/512 maskable icons

Screens:
- /         Landing: hero, value prop, daily-stat strip, footer disclaimer
- /checkin  Camera capture via real getUserMedia, faint face-guide oval,
            simulated 1.8s analyze step routes to /result
- /result   Score hero with count-up animation, five-axis SVG radar with
            confidence bands, tiered plan (1hr/1day free; 7d/30d locked
            behind paywall per freemium gating decision), disclaimer + request_id

Components:
- AxisRadar       SVG, low-opacity rose polygon + semantic axis-color dots
- ScoreNumber     count-up to value over 600ms easeOutCubic
- PlanTier        collapsible cards with axis-color dots, lock icon for paid
- ui/Button       cva variants (primary/rose/ghost/link), four sizes
- ui/Card         the single card primitive

What's stubbed (documented in web/README.md):
- lib/mock-data.ts holds a hard-coded MirrorResponse
- HAS_SUBSCRIPTION constant gates the paid tiers
- /checkin submit simulates the agent loop with setTimeout

Build verified: pnpm typecheck clean, pnpm build green on all routes
(~104KB First Load JS), all three routes return 200 on `pnpm start`.

Out of scope (v0.2 build, not scaffold): Supabase auth, Stripe Checkout,
history page, web push, service worker, real image upload pipeline.

commit.message:
Real-photo manifest schema + contributor flow (v0.1.1 item 6)

- evals/golden_set/PHOTOS.md: per-photo checklist (source, license,
  EXIF strip, resolution, manifest entry, human labels) for replacing
  synthetic placeholders with real selfies one at a time.
- Manifest schema extended (backward compatible) with is_real_photo,
  attribution {source, photo_url, photographer, license},
  human_labeled_at, human_labeler. llm_judge documents the new fields
  and ignores unknowns so older entries keep working.
- README updated for the v0.1.1 surface: transport flag, adversarial
  run, trace observability viewer, CI workflow, real-photo flow.

Network policy in this environment blocks all photo CDNs, so the
fixtures stay synthetic for now; you drop photos in and the harness
plugs them in. Image IDs are never reused (audit log references them).

commit.message:
CI regression workflow + trace observability viewer (v0.1.1 items 4 + 5)

- .github/workflows/regression.yml: every PR and main-branch push runs
  unit tests, mock golden-set regression, and mock adversarial regression
  (must catch 10/10). A separate \"live\" job runs against the real
  Anthropic API when the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret is configured; skipped
  on forks for safety.
- src/observability/viewer.py: read-only CLI over traces/ (and the
  append-only audit log). Filters by status, request_id, or
  medical_advice_flag=true. --show <id> dumps the full trace.

Together: every commit is provably passing both the score-validity bar
and the no-medical-advice bar at merge time, and any prod incident is
one grep away from a full trace.

commit.message:
Append-only audit log of every shipped response (v0.1.1 item 3)

- src/orchestration/audit_log.py: JSONL daily files under audit/, written
  via O_APPEND + fsync per record. Hashes only (image hash + response
  hash); no PII, no image bytes. PRD-compliant data minimization (§8.5).
- Orchestrator appends one record on every successful run, immediately
  before returning the response. Errors and blocks don't pollute the log.
- search() supports filtering by request_id, user_id,
  medical_advice_flag, and a since-date; sufficient until we have ~1M
  records, after which this moves to SQLite or a managed log.
- Liability defense: when a user complains \"your app told me X on
  date D\", we can produce the exact response that left our system in
  one grep. GDPR right-to-delete tombstones the user-side mapping but
  keeps the hash trail for our defense.
- audit/ gitignored; in prod this writes to durable storage with object
  lock or an append-only DB.
- tests/test_audit_log.py covers write-through, durable append (two
  records in one file), and the search filters.

commit.message:
Production Anthropic API transport + --transport flag (v0.1.1 item 2)

- AnthropicAPIClient: drop-in replacement for ClaudeClient that hits the
  Anthropic Messages API directly. Same async interface (system, user_text,
  image_path, model) -> LLMResult, so the orchestrator is transport-agnostic.
- build_transport() factory selects between mock / max / api. CLI and
  both regression runners now take --transport; --live remains as a
  deprecated alias mapping to --transport=max.
- Image input on the API transport goes inline as a content block,
  bypassing the claude-agent-sdk Read-tool workaround. Cheaper, faster,
  and what we'll use at GA.
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY required for api transport; fails fast if missing.
- tests/test_transport.py covers all three factory branches plus the
  missing-key failure.

This is the swap path documented in PRD: Max plan for dev, Anthropic API
for multi-tenant prod. UI build can target the prod transport from day 1.

commit.message:
Adversarial regression + hard-block integration test (v0.1.1 item 1)

- 10 adversarial fixtures spanning every violation class the EvalCritic
  is supposed to catch: named conditions (acne, rosacea, eczema),
  prescription products (tretinoin, accutane, hydroquinone), mole/lesion
  references, treatment/diagnose/disease language, and stacked
  violations. Each MUST set medical_advice_flag=true; 10/10 pass
  in mock mode (TNR=1.0).
- evals/adversarial_run.py is the runner; non-zero exit on any miss so
  it slots into CI alongside regression_run.
- tests/test_hard_block.py: parametrized over every BLOCKED_TERM, with
  a fail-open mock LLM judge. Proves the deterministic guard catches
  the violation even when the model-side judge silently passes a bad
  response. Also includes the disclaimer-doesn't-self-trip regression.
- README in evals/adversarial/ documenting why this exists: defensible
  evidence for FTC / FDA / state-AG / plaintiff questions about how we
  verified the medical-advice boundary.

Wire live mode through claude-agent-sdk; promote EvalCritic to Opus 4.7

- Live transport: claude-agent-sdk's prompt arg is string-only, so the
  inline-image content-block path hung the SDK. Switched to writing the
  resolved image path into the prompt and granting the Read tool so
  Claude loads bytes itself. Bumped per-call max_turns (15 vision / 4
  text) to absorb tool round-trips.
- Tolerant JSON extractor (src/orchestration/json_extract.py) used by all
  three agents: brace-counted, fence-stripped, ignores trailing prose.
  Verified end-to-end live run on case_01 (real Sonnet vision call:
  honestly returned low confidence on the synthetic fixture).
- EvalCritic promoted from Haiku 4.5 to Opus 4.7. Judge is the runtime
  guardrail for medical-advice violations; a false negative is a
  regulatory incident, so paying Opus prices here is correct. Producer
  agents (Skin / Recommendation) stay on Sonnet / Haiku.
- Per-request cost cap raised 0.05 -> 0.15 to fit Opus judge.
- PRD cost envelope updated (~$0.014 -> ~$0.046/request, ~430/mo at cap).

commit.message:
Scaffold MirrorScore v0.1: 3-agent ReAct loop + eval harness

- PRD defending 3 LLM agents (Skin / Recommendation / EvalCritic) plus a
  deterministic ImageQuality preprocessor and an Orchestrator harness.
- Agents back to claude-agent-sdk so calls bill against the active
  Claude Max plan; no API key required. Mock mode is the harness default.
- Pydantic response/trace contracts; plan items must cite emitted axes
  and glow_score is bounded to within +/-15 of the axis mean.
- ReAct orchestrator: linear happy path, single retry on EvalCritic flag,
  per-call trace with model/tokens/cost/latency/rationale.
- Eval harness across output / trajectory / trace / golden-judge surfaces;
  exits non-zero on any failure.
- 5 synthetic golden fixtures (clearly labeled test_fixture: true) plus
  generator script; regression_run is green end-to-end in mock mode.
- pytest suite (9 tests) covering schemas, image quality, orchestrator
  happy path and trace completeness.
